newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends up for third straight day.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends up for third straight day.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed up 60 basis points at 24.80 percent, their third consecutive gain, after zigzagging through a session fraught by speculation in the wake of volatile international markets, traders said.
"Although the system was supposed to be liquid, some are still witholding their cash, and the fact that the central bank is draining liquidity helps them," a trader said.
Banco de Mexico drained 1.602 billion pesos of liquidity by offering to purchase paper through three auctions on the secondary market.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed up 65 basis points at 25.75 percent.
Dealers noted that volatility in yields on U.S. long bonds triggered jitters and instability in the foreign exchange market which thus affected the money market.
Other traders said secondary rates were gaining on a technical adjustment.
"Some big banks sold paper at the beginning of the week, when secondary rates fell substantially, and now they're climbing back up," another dealer said.
No credit maturities were expected for Monday, however, 602 million pesos was expected to return to the system following Friday's central bank intervention.
